member_targets: Practical methods or techniques that improve reliable recognition of planned checkpoints under degraded visibility or difficult terrain conditions.
Preparatory measures or techniques a field team can adopt in advance so that planned checkpoints remain identifiable under poor-visibility conditions.
Practical methods or techniques a field team can use to make planned checkpoints identifiable under degraded weather or visibility conditions.
Techniques or criteria by which field teams select and recognize suitable checkpoint landmarks in terrain they have not previously traveled.
The set of techniques or procedures by which field teams select landmarks/checkpoints and confirm that a feature encountered is the intended checkpoint.
The specific alternate route to be used for a given leg under changed conditions — a particular routing choice, which the passage does not supply for any concrete journey.

The specific alternate routes recorded for legs of a particular planned journey, to be used when a checkpoint cannot be recognized — i.e., the identity of contingency route options, not the general practice of recording alternates.

The specific alternate routes designated for use when a planned checkpoint cannot be recognized — i.e., the content of the contingency route options for particular legs, which the passage describes only generically as 'an alternate if conditions change'.

The specific content of the contingency/alternate routes or actions teams adopt when a planned checkpoint cannot be recognized — i.e., what the alternates consist of, not merely that alternates are recorded.

The specific contingency routes or alternate legs a team should prepare for use when a planned checkpoint cannot be identified — i.e., prescriptive content of the alternates, not merely the fact that alternates are recorded.
The specific alternate route(s) recorded for a leg, to be used when a checkpoint becomes unrecognizable under changed conditions.
The specific alternate routes recorded for each leg of a particular team's journey plan, to be used if conditions change.

The specific alternate route or path the team should follow when a planned checkpoint cannot be recognized — a particular routing decision that depends on leg-specific details (the actual checkpoints, terrain, and pre-recorded alternates) not given in the passage.
The specific alternate route to be followed in place of the planned leg when a checkpoint cannot be recognized.
The specific alternate routes recorded for a leg, to be used as contingency when a planned checkpoint cannot be recognized.

The method or basis by which field teams arrive at the expected distance or travel time figure for a leg (i.e., how those estimates are produced), which the passage states is recorded but does not explain.
The set of causal factors, ranked by frequency of occurrence, that make a planned checkpoint unexpectedly difficult to recognize in the field.

The relative frequency ranking of specific causes (e.g., weather, visibility, terrain, approach direction, or others) that lead field teams to fail to recognize a planned checkpoint — i.e., which factors are most common, not merely which ones can contribute.
The set of specific conditions or causes—and their relative frequency—that most often make a planned checkpoint unrecognizable in the field.
The set of specific causes, ranked by frequency of occurrence, that make a planned checkpoint difficult to recognize in the field

The identification of which particular conditions or causes are the most frequent contributors to a planned checkpoint being unexpectedly difficult to recognize — i.e., a ranked or relative-frequency account of recognition-failure factors, not merely a list of possible influences.
The specific causal factors that most frequently lead field teams to misidentify a planned checkpoint, ranked by relative frequency of occurrence.
The set of specific conditions or causes, ranked by frequency of occurrence, that lead field teams to fail to recognize a planned checkpoint when approaching it.
The set of specific conditions or causes that most frequently make a pre-planned checkpoint difficult to recognize during field travel, ranked or identified by relative frequency.
The set of specific conditions or causes, ranked by frequency of occurrence, that lead field teams to fail to recognize a planned checkpoint.

The relative frequency ranking of specific causes of checkpoint non-recognition — i.e., which factors (among weather, visibility, terrain, approach direction, or others) most often prevent a team from identifying a planned checkpoint upon arrival.
The set of specific conditions or causes, ranked by frequency of occurrence in practice, that make a planned checkpoint hard to recognize in the field.

The empirically observed relative frequency ranking of causes that render a planned checkpoint unrecognizable in field practice — i.e., which specific factors most commonly produce recognition failure despite careful planning.
The set of specific conditions or causes that most frequently make a planned checkpoint hard to recognize in the field, ranked or characterized by relative frequency.

The identity and relative frequency of the particular causes that most commonly render a planned checkpoint unrecognizable on arrival — i.e., a ranked/empirical account of which factors (beyond the passage's general list of weather, visibility, terrain, approach direction) predominate in practice.

The empirical ranking/frequency of the particular causes (e.g., weather, visibility, terrain, approach direction, or others) that most commonly render a planned checkpoint unrecognizable in actual field practice.

focal_unknown_anchor: When a checkpoint becomes hard to recognize, the critical navigation decision is how long to continue toward it before abandoning that leg for an alternate route.
